theme: The Periodic Table, Elements & Chemical Reactions
title: The Periodic Table, Elements & Chemical Reactions
description: A 60-question grand master assessment exploring Mendeleev periodic law, alkali and transition metals, carbon allotropes, bonding, acid-base dynamics, and superheavy elements.

questions.question: What Russian chemist formulated the first Periodic Law in 1869, arranging elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps to predict undiscovered elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev accurately predicted the existence and physical properties of undiscovered elements including gallium (eka-aluminum) and germanium (eka-silicon).

questions.question: What British physicist demonstrated in 1913 using X-ray emission spectroscopy that the periodic table is fundamentally ordered by atomic number nuclear charge?
questions.explanation: Moseley Law showed that X-ray frequency is proportional to atomic number $Z$, correctly ordering elements like tellurium and iodine regardless of atomic mass.

questions.question: What term designates the horizontal rows in the modern periodic table, corresponding directly to the principal quantum electron shell number?
questions.explanation: There are currently seven periods in the periodic table, ranging from period 1 (holding only H and He) to period 7 (ending at element 118, Oganesson).

questions.question: What term designates the 18 vertical columns in the periodic table, grouping elements with identical numbers of valence electrons?
questions.explanation: Elements in the same IUPAC group (e.g. Group 1 alkali metals, Group 17 halogens) share similar valence shell configurations and chemical reactivity.

questions.question: What periodic trend describes the minimum energy required to remove the most loosely held valence electron from an isolated gaseous atom?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period from left to right due to increasing effective nuclear charge and decreases down a group due to electron shielding.

questions.question: How many officially verified and IUPAC-recognized chemical elements make up the modern complete Periodic Table from Hydrogen to Oganesson?
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table contains exactly 118 confirmed elements, completed across all seven periods with the formal naming of elements 113, 115, 117, and 118 in 2016.

questions.question: What Group 1 alkali metal is the least dense solid metal element at standard conditions, floating easily on water and mineral oil?
questions.explanation: Lithium has a density of only 0.534 g/cm3, roughly half the density of water, possessing the highest electrochemical reduction potential.

questions.question: Why must pure elemental alkali metals like sodium, potassium, and cesium be stored submerged in dry mineral oil or sealed in inert argon glass ampoules?
options: They react violently and exothermically with atmospheric moisture and oxygen
They sublimate directly into toxic vapors
questions.explanation: Alkali metals have a single $s^1$ valence electron that is readily lost, reacting exothermically with water to produce caustic metal hydroxides and flammable hydrogen gas.

questions.question: What intense characteristic flame test emission color is produced when sodium metal or its salts are vaporized in a Bunsen burner flame?
questions.explanation: Thermally excited valence electrons in sodium relax from the 3p to 3s orbital, emitting iconic yellow doublet spectral lines at 589.0 and 589.6 nanometers.

questions.question: What Group 2 alkaline earth metal with atomic number 12 burns with a blinding, brilliant white light used in maritime flares and pyrotechnics?
questions.explanation: Magnesium reacts vigorously with oxygen at high temperatures to form magnesium oxide ($MgO$), emitting intense ultraviolet and visible white light.

questions.question: What alkali metal in period 6 has a low melting point of just 28.5 °C, melting in human hand temperature and reacting explosively with cold water?
questions.explanation: Cesium has a large atomic radius and weak metallic bonding, making it extremely soft with a melting point of 28.5 °C and the highest chemical reactivity of stable metals.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Hydrogen, the lightest element and most abundant atomic substance in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has atomic number 1, consisting of a single proton and single electron (in protium), making up over 73 percent of the baryonic mass of the universe.

questions.question: What transition metal element with atomic number 26 is the most abundant element by mass in planet Earth as a whole, concentrated heavily in the core?
questions.explanation: Iron constitutes approximately 32.1% of Earth total mass (mostly in the core) and forms the backbone of global steel infrastructure.

questions.question: What transition metal element possesses the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal at standard room temperature?
questions.explanation: Silver has an electrical conductivity of $6.30 \times 10^7$ S/m, slightly outperforming copper, though copper is more widely used due to lower cost.

questions.question: What transition metal element has the highest melting point of any pure metal in the Periodic Table at an extraordinary 3,422 degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: Tungsten (Wolfram, W) has half-filled $5d$ and $6s$ valence electron states that create exceptionally strong covalent-like metallic bonds in its crystal lattice.

questions.question: What dense transition metal is the only pure metallic element that exists in a liquid state at standard room temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Relativistic contraction of the 6s electron shell in mercury atoms stabilizes the closed-shell configuration, weakening metallic bonding so it melts at -38.8 °C.

questions.question: What precious transition metal element with atomic number 79 is the most malleable and ductile metal known, able to be beaten into sheets 400 times thinner than hair?
questions.explanation: A single gram of pure gold can be hammered into a one-square-meter sheet of translucent gold leaf or drawn into a wire over two kilometers long.

questions.question: What is the melting point in degrees Celsius of the refractory transition metal Tungsten W, the highest melting point of any metal?
questions.explanation: Tungsten possesses the highest melting point of all pure metals at 3,422 °C (3,695 Kelvin), widely used in incandescent filaments, rocket nozzles, and welding electrodes.

questions.question: What Group 17 halogen gas is the most chemically reactive and electronegative element in the entire Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has a Pauling electronegativity of 3.98, reacting aggressively with virtually all other elements (including water, glass, and noble gases like xenon).

questions.question: What dense, fuming reddish-brown halogen is the only non-metallic element that exists as a liquid at standard room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine (Br2) boils at 58.8 °C and freezes at -7.2 °C, giving off pungent, corrosive reddish vapors that attack mucous membranes.

questions.question: What Group 18 noble gas was first discovered by astronomers in the solar spectrum during an 1868 eclipse before being found on Earth?
questions.explanation: Pierre Janssen and Norman Lockyer identified a yellow spectral line (D3) in solar prominences, naming the element Helium after the Greek sun god Helios.

questions.question: What foundational chemical rule states that main-group atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to attain a stable valence configuration of eight electrons?
questions.explanation: Formulated by Gilbert Lewis, the octet rule reflects the thermodynamic stability of completely filled $s^2 p^6$ valence electron configurations like noble gases.

questions.question: What radioactive, dense noble gas element accumulates in building basements from the natural decay chain of uranium in granite rocks and soils?
questions.explanation: Radon-222 is an alpha-emitting radioactive gas with a 3.8-day half-life, representing the second leading cause of lung cancer after tobacco smoking.

questions.question: What is the highest Pauling scale electronegativity value in chemistry, held by the element Fluorine?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of any element at 3.98 on the Pauling scale, defining the upper benchmark of atomic electron attraction.

questions.question: What unique chemical capability of carbon allows it to form strong, stable covalent bonds with other carbon atoms to build infinite chains and rings?
questions.explanation: High carbon-carbon bond enthalpy (347 kJ/mol) combined with tetravalence allows carbon to build the millions of complex molecules that form organic life.

questions.question: What carbon allotrope consists of a single atom-thick two-dimensional sheet of sp2 carbon atoms in a hexagonal honeycomb lattice, stronger than steel?
questions.explanation: Isolated in 2004 by Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov (2010 Nobel Prize), graphene has extraordinary electrical mobility and 200-times steel tensile strength.

questions.question: What spherical carbon cage molecule composed of 60 carbon atoms in truncated icosahedron rings resembles a geometric soccer ball?
questions.explanation: Discovered by Kroto, Curl, and Smalley in 1985 (1996 Nobel Prize), fullerenes opened the field of carbon nanotechnology and supramolecular chemistry.

questions.question: What soft, grey-black carbon allotrope consists of stacked graphene layers held together by weak van der Waals forces, making it an excellent dry lubricant?
questions.explanation: Delocalized pi electrons in graphite sheets allow it to conduct electricity, while easy sliding between adjacent layers makes it soft enough for pencil leads.

questions.question: What major branch of chemistry is dedicated exclusively to the study of carbon-containing compounds, structures, and reaction mechanisms?
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry investigates the synthesis, stereochemistry, and reactivity of hydrocarbons and their functional group derivatives in biology and materials.

questions.question: How many valence electrons does a neutral ground-state Carbon atom possess in its outer shell, enabling tetravalent bonding?
questions.explanation: Carbon (atomic number 6) has an electron configuration of $1s^2 2s^2 2p^2$, providing exactly four valence electrons that form $sp^3, sp^2$, or $sp$ hybrid orbitals.

questions.question: What series of 15 f-block metallic elements spanning atomic numbers 57 to 71 is critical for neodymium super-magnets, lasers, and smartphones?
questions.explanation: Lanthanides fill the 4f electron subshell, exhibiting the Lanthanide Contraction which causes atomic radii to decrease smoothly across the row.

questions.question: What naturally occurring radioactive actinide isotope is the primary fissile fuel enriched for commercial nuclear power reactors?
questions.explanation: Uranium-235 undergoes induced nuclear fission when struck by a thermal neutron, releasing 200 MeV of energy and 2 to 3 prompt neutrons per fission.

questions.question: What synthetic radioactive actinide element named after the Americas was created in 1944 and is utilized in household ionization smoke detectors?
questions.explanation: Americium-241 emits alpha particles that ionize air molecules inside a chamber; smoke particles interrupt the electric current, triggering the alarm.

questions.question: What physical parameter defines the exact time required for one-half of the radioactive nuclei in an unstable radioisotope sample to decay?
questions.explanation: Described by exponential decay law $N(t) = N_0 (1/2)^{t/t_{1/2}}$, half-lives range from fractions of a microsecond to billions of years (e.g., U-238: 4.5 billion years).

questions.question: Who is the only scientist in history to receive Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields, Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911), for discovering radium and polonium?
questions.explanation: Marie Sklodowska Curie coined the term radioactivity, developed mobile X-ray units during WWI, and isolated pure radium metal.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of Uranium, the heaviest naturally occurring primordial chemical element on the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Uranium has atomic number 92; all elements with higher atomic numbers ($Z \ge 93$) are synthetic transuranic elements created in nuclear reactors or accelerators.

questions.question: What type of chemical bond forms from the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged cations and anions after electron transfer?
questions.explanation: Ionic bonds typically form between elements with large electronegativity differences ($Delta EN > 2.0$), such as sodium and chlorine in table salt crystals.

questions.question: What chemical bond is formed when two non-metal atoms share pairs of valence electrons to achieve stable noble-gas electron configurations?
questions.explanation: Covalent bonds involve overlapping atomic orbitals, forming sigma and pi bonding molecular orbitals that hold molecules together.

questions.question: What chemical model predicts three-dimensional molecular geometries by minimizing electrostatic repulsion between bonding and lone electron pairs?
questions.explanation: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion VSEPR predicts linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, and octahedral molecular shapes.

questions.question: What strong dipole-dipole intermolecular attraction occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to highly electronegative nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding gives liquid water its unusually high boiling point, surface tension, and expanded density structure when freezing into ice.

questions.question: What bond angle in degrees characterizes the perfect tetrahedral molecular geometry of a methane molecule (CH4)?
questions.explanation: Four equivalent $sp^3$ hybrid orbital bonding pairs orient to maximize spatial separation in 3D, creating the classic 109.5-degree tetrahedral angle.

questions.question: What is the measured bond angle in degrees between the two hydrogen-oxygen bonds in a bent liquid water molecule H2O?
questions.explanation: The two non-bonding lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom exert greater electrostatic repulsion than bonding pairs, compressing the tetrahedral angle from 109.5° down to 104.5°.

questions.question: According to the Bronsted-Lowry acid-base theory, how is an acid fundamentally defined in chemical reactions?
options: A chemical species that donates a proton H+
questions.explanation: In the Bronsted-Lowry model, an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor, forming conjugate acid-base pairs.

questions.question: What logarithmic scale devised by Soren Sorensen in 1909 measures the hydrogen ion concentration ($-\log_{10}[H^+]$) of an aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Because the pH scale is logarithmic, each unit change represents a 10-fold change in acidity (e.g. pH 3 is ten times more acidic than pH 4).

questions.question: What is the exact pH value of pure neutral water at standard room temperature of 25 degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: At 25 °C, the autoionization constant of water $K_w = 1.0 \times 10^{-14}$, making $[H^+] = [OH^-] = 1.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M, which yields pH 7.0.

questions.question: What solution containing a weak acid and its conjugate base resists changes in pH when small amounts of strong acid or base are added?
questions.explanation: Buffers like the carbonic acid-bicarbonate system in human blood ($H_2CO_3 / HCO_3^-$) maintain blood pH tightly between 7.35 and 7.45.

questions.question: What quantitative analytical laboratory method determines the unknown concentration of an acid by neutralizing it with a standardized base solution?
questions.explanation: In a titration, a buret delivers titrant into an analyte solution until a chemical indicator or pH meter detects the stoichiometric equivalence point.

questions.question: What is the pH value of pure neutral distilled water at standard room temperature 25 °C?
questions.explanation: At standard room temperature (25 °C), pure water has equal concentrations of $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions ($10^{-7}$ M), yielding a neutral pH of exactly 7.0.

questions.question: What minimum energy barrier must colliding reactant molecules overcome in order to break bonds and reach the transition state in a reaction?
questions.explanation: According to the Arrhenius equation $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$, reaction rates increase exponentially with temperature as more molecules surpass activation energy.

questions.question: What substance speeds up the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy without being consumed?
questions.explanation: Catalysts increase both forward and reverse reaction rates equally without altering the chemical equilibrium position or Gibbs free energy.

questions.question: What thermodynamic state function measures the degree of molecular disorder, randomness, or dispersal of energy microstates in a system?
questions.explanation: The Second Law of Thermodynamics states that the total entropy of an isolated system always increases over time ($Delta S_{univ} > 0$ for spontaneous processes).

questions.question: What chemical principle states that when a dynamic equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, temperature, or pressure, the system shifts to counteract it?
questions.explanation: Discovered by Henri Le Chatelier in 1884, this principle allows chemical engineers to maximize ammonia yields in the Haber-Bosch process.

questions.question: What type of chemical reaction releases thermal heat energy to the surroundings, exhibiting a negative enthalpy change ($Delta H < 0$)?
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions, like hydrocarbon combustion and acid-base neutralizations, release energy because product bonds are stronger than reactant bonds.

questions.question: What is the power of 10 exponent value n in Avogadro number 6.022 x 10^n particles per mole?
questions.explanation: Avogadro constant $N_A = 6.02214076 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$ defines the exact number of constituent particles (atoms, molecules) in one mole of substance.

questions.question: What superheavy synthetic noble gas element with atomic number 118 completes the seventh period of the Periodic Table, named after physicist Yuri Oganessian?
questions.explanation: Oganesson was synthesized at the Flerov Laboratory in Dubna, Russia by bombarding Californium-249 targets with accelerated Calcium-48 ions.

questions.question: What theoretical region of the nuclear chart predicts that certain superheavy nuclei with magic numbers of protons and neutrons may exhibit longer half-lives?
questions.explanation: Glenn Seaborg predicted that closed nuclear shells around $Z=114-126$ and $N=184$ would dramatically slow alpha decay, potentially yielding longer-lived superheavy atoms.

questions.question: What superheavy halogen element with atomic number 117 was synthesized jointly by Russian and American scientists, named after the US state of Tennessee?
questions.explanation: Tennessine was officially named in 2016 in recognition of the contributions of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Vanderbilt University, and UT Knoxville.

questions.question: What heavy ion particle projectile ($Z=20, A=48$) with neutron-rich magic structure is widely used in cyclotrons to synthesize superheavy elements?
questions.explanation: Calcium-48 is a doubly-magic isotope (20 protons, 28 neutrons) that provides extra nuclear stability during fusion collisions with actinide targets.

questions.question: What superheavy element with atomic number 115 was officially named after the Moscow Oblast region where the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research is located?
questions.explanation: Element 115 was officially named Moscovium by IUPAC in 2016 to honor the ancient Russian region hosting the Dubna synthesis experiments.

questions.question: What is the highest atomic number element currently synthesized, verified, and officially named on the modern Periodic Table Oganesson?
questions.explanation: Oganesson ($Z=118$) occupies the final position in Period 7 and Group 18, representing the highest atomic number element verified to date.
